hints: Evaluate $\int x^2\ln x\,dx$ by parts, choosing $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x^2\,dx$.
Use $du=dx/x$ and $v=x^3/3$ to complete the antiderivative before applying any limits.
Evaluate the antiderivative at $a$ and $1$, then set the result equal to $4$.
Multiply through to collect the terms containing $a^3$, isolate $a^3$, and finally take the real cube root to reach the required fixed-point form.
walkthrough:
Use integration by parts $\int u\,\mathrm{d}v = uv - \int v\,\mathrm{d}u$ to evaluate the integral $\int_1^a x^2\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x$:
Let $u = \ln x$ and $\mathrm{d}v = x^2\,\mathrm{d}x$, which gives $\mathrm{d}u = \dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x$ and $v = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3$.

Apply the integration by parts formula:
$$\int x^2\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3\ln x - \int \dfrac{1}{3}x^3\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3\ln x - \dfrac{1}{3}\int x^2\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Complete the integration of the remaining term:
$$\int x^2\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3\ln x - \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x^3\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3\ln x - \dfrac{1}{9}x^3$$

Substitute the integration limits from $1$ to $a$:
$$\left[ \dfrac{1}{3}x^3\ln x - \dfrac{1}{9}x^3 \right]_1^a = \left( \dfrac{1}{3}a^3\ln a - \dfrac{1}{9}a^3 \right) - \left( \dfrac{1}{3}(1)^3\ln(1) - \dfrac{1}{9}(1)^3 \right)$$

Equate the value of the integral to $4$:
$$\dfrac{1}{3}a^3\ln a - \dfrac{1}{9}a^3 + \dfrac{1}{9} = 4$$

Multiply through by $9$ to eliminate denominators:
$$3a^3\ln a - a^3 + 1 = 36$$
$$3a^3\ln a - a^3 = 35$$
$$a^3(3\ln a - 1) = 35$$

Isolate $a^3$ and take the cube root to obtain the required formula:
$$a^3 = \dfrac{35}{3\ln a - 1}$$
$$a = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln a - 1} \right)^{1/3}$$

hints: Use the fixed-point equation from part (a) to define $g(x)=\left(\dfrac{35}{3\ln x-1}\right)^{1/3}$.
Calculate $g(2.4)$ and $g(2.8)$, keeping enough decimal places for a clear comparison.
Show that $g(2.4)$ lies above $2.4$ while $g(2.8)$ lies below $2.8$; equivalently, show that $g(x)-x$ changes sign across the interval.
walkthrough: Define the fixed-point iteration function $g(x) = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln x - 1} \right)^{1/3}$ and the function $f(x) = g(x) - x$.
Conclude that because $f(x)$ is continuous on $[2.4, 2.8]$ and $f(2.4) > 0$ while $f(2.8) < 0$ (a change in sign), the root $a$ must lie between $2.4$ and $2.8$.

hints: Use the equation from part (a) as the iteration $a_{n+1}=\left(\dfrac{35}{3\ln a_n-1}\right)^{1/3}$.
Choose a starting value within the verified interval $2.4<a<2.8$ and evaluate the natural logarithm at each step.
Record every iterate to 4 decimal places, continuing until successive values stabilise sufficiently to justify the same value to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Set up the iterative formula based on part (a):
$$a_{n+1} = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln a_n - 1} \right)^{1/3}$$

Choose an initial approximation in the interval $[2.4, 2.8]$, such as $a_0 = 2.6$, and compute successive iterations to 4 decimal places:
$$a_1 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6567$$
$$a_2 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6567) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6267$$
$$a_3 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6267) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6423$$
$$a_4 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6423) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6341$$
$$a_5 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6341) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6384$$
$$a_6 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6384) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6362$$
$$a_7 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6362) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6373$$
$$a_8 = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln(2.6373) - 1} \right)^{1/3} \approx 2.6367$$

Verify the rounding to 2 decimal places by checking the sign of $f(x) = \left( \dfrac{35}{3\ln x - 1} \right)^{1/3} - x$ at the boundaries $2.635$ and $2.645$:
$$f(2.635) \approx 2.6379 - 2.635 = +0.0029 > 0$$
$$f(2.645) \approx 2.6327 - 2.645 = -0.0123 < 0$$

Since there is a sign change across the interval $(2.635, 2.645)$, conclude that $a$ rounds to:
$$a = 2.64$$
